reviews.review:
Released in 2013, Risk of Rain really brought the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ heat when it comes to roguelites while looking like something you'd expect to see in those dinosaur consoles.

RoR was made by two students from the University of Washington who wanted to combine two of their favorite genres, platformers and roguelikes, mixed with this concept they've been tinkering about raising the difficulty over time. 

They initially made a tower defense game, using enemy AI to "buy" enemies and raise the AI's difficulty over time. When that didn't make their nipples hard, they decided to take this concept, upgrade it, and test it on a platformer called Risk of Rain. 

They knew this 8-bit two-dimensional game had potential. They even noticed that certain item combinations can cause the player to essentially become a god. Still, they deemed it acceptable since the game's RNG mechanics evened out the odds. The feeling you get when you get your first god-run is knee-slapping good. In the later series, they included an option to choose your items during your run, which makes trying out different synergies super efficient at the expense of making your run a little "easier" and potentially less fun due to the lack of item RNG.

With the game nearly finished and them spending all the money they had towards the game, the boys opened a Kickstarter to raise funds to really slap ass with this game. They initially just wanted $7,000, but in the end, they raised a little over $30,000 whopping dollars with nearly 1,700 backers.

The game was released on Steam in early November 2013, a perfect time for youngins like myself back then to buy trending games with Christmas money. Throughout its lifetime, the game's Steam sales generated nearly $10,000,000 in Gross Revenue, and the boys even managed to keep $3,000,000 after paying taxes, refunds, and Steam cuts, according to Steam-revenue-calculator.com. Wild. 

I played this game with my childhood best friend during my early high school years. We'd take turns playing runs and seeing who can get the coolest synergies and combos. I'd spent many afternoons and nights on this game. I worried they'd ruin my comfort game when I heard that RoR 2 was being developed and they were making it three-dimensional. That's how much I cared about this 8-bit game when other hits like GTA 5, The Last of Us, and BioShock Infinite came out during the same year.

Highly recommend but you should probably just get Risk of Rain Returns if you want an updated or "modern" feel.
